title: “Someone asked me and pointed out to me today that I show my face when I share about Jesus.”
paragraphs: “Someone asked me and pointed out to me today that I show my face when I share about Jesus.”
And I want to answer that with clarity and humility.

I don’t show my face to be praised.
I don’t show my face to build a platform.
I don’t show my face because the message is about me.
I show my face because faith is personal, conviction is costly, and truth deserves accountability.

The Bible says, “He must increase, but I must decrease.” (John 3:30)
That verse doesn’t mean we disappear — it means Jesus remains the focus, even while we stand openly in our faith.

Scripture also says, “Let your light shine before others, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father in heaven.” (Matthew 5:16)
Notice who gets the glory — not the vessel, but the Father.

I don’t want anyone copying my words or my walk.
I want people to seek their own relationship with Christ, rooted in Scripture and led by the Spirit.

Paul said it best:
“Follow me as I follow Christ.” (1 Corinthians 11:1)

If my face is visible, let it only serve as a reminder that the gospel isn’t anonymous — it’s lived.
And if anything I share ever points more to me than to Jesus, then I’ve missed the point completely.
